title: Leadership Exact Payment
description: While another player resolves a strategy card, a follower can prepare the Leadership secondary: the tokens to buy, their pools and now the exact payment (which planets are exhausted, how many trade goods are spent), chosen on the map exactly as in the real flow. Before, only the tokens and pools were kept and the payment was planned by Auto-pay when the real question opened. The engine's payment is the player's own choice, one planet or trade good per question, so the exact payment can be prepared: the server replays the whole scripted purchase (payment, pool, 'again?') through the engine's own flow, read only, and the real question later validates it. The before shots are taken on the commit without the exact payment and committed; the after shots are regenerated by npm run screenshots -- AU. Synthetic fixtures through a mocked server, not captured engine states.

shots.heading: Before: paying on the map in preparation
shots.caption: The real map payment is available in prepare mode, with the planets ringed and the bar covering the bill, but the choice made here (Jord and Quann instead of Auto-pay's Lodor) was thrown away on Save: only the tokens and their pools went into the plan.

shots.heading: After: the same choice is the plan
shots.caption: Same screen, same controls. The banner now says the game checks the whole purchase, payment included, when it is saved and again when the turn comes. Confirm records the planets and trade goods by meaning (planet ids and a trade-good count), asks the engine to replay the purchase read only, and spends nothing.

shots.heading: Before: the saved plan names no payment
shots.caption: The chip reads 'Buy 1 command token (1 fleet)': what would be paid was left for arrival.

shots.heading: After: the saved plan names the payment
shots.caption: The chip reads '... paying Jord, Quann'. Trade goods appear the same way ('paying Jord, 1 trade good'). Older saved plans without a payment keep working: Auto-pay plans them at arrival, as before.

shots.heading: Before: arrival (Review) opens an empty panel
shots.caption: The Prepared bar says what is bought but not how it is paid, and the panel opened with nothing staged: the payment that would go out was Auto-pay's, not the player's choice.

shots.heading: After: arrival opens with the payment selected
shots.caption: The usual panel opens with the prepared purchase staged: one token bought, the fleet pool, and Jord and Quann marked as the payment ('Your own choice'). The bar says 'paying Jord, Quann' and one Confirm sends exactly that through the normal token batch. Auto sends the same after its visible delay.

shots.heading: Before: a planet exhausted meanwhile goes unnoticed
shots.caption: Jord was exhausted by someone else before the window opened. The bar looks exactly as if nothing had changed (Buy 1 command token, no payment named): what would go out is whatever Auto-pay finds now, with nothing to tell the player that the plan's planet is gone.

shots.heading: After: Needs review with the reason
shots.caption: A payment that no longer fits (a planet exhausted or taken, trade goods spent, the bill no longer covered) is not sent: Needs review names it, says what Auto-pay would use instead and has that replacement selected in the panel for one click.

shots.heading: Variant: the engine does not offer the chosen payment
shots.caption: When the engine's own flow would not offer a step of the scripted payment as of now, nothing is saved and the bar and the banner say which step; what was staged stays so it can be changed. If the engine cannot answer (older server, rate limit) the payment is saved unchecked and validated at arrival.

notes.title: Is the payment a choice?
notes.text: Yes. The engine pays Leadership's influence one planet or trade good per question (pay_influence, each option with its worth), with no automatic rule; only a lone option is taken without asking. So the exact payment is the player's, and it is what is prepared. Unlike Technology (where the engine applies the first payment plan and the preview only reads it), nothing is invented here.

notes.title: How the check works.
notes.text: The preview now takes the whole scripted purchase (the window's yes, each payment, each token's pool, 'yes' between tokens) and replays it through the engine's own follow flow on a throwaway copy. It answers with the next question, 'complete', or 'rejected' naming the answer that is not offered. Read only: no live game, RNG, log or storage is touched; same privacy and rate limits.

notes.title: What can change before the window.
notes.text: Planets exhausted by the primary or earlier followers, trade goods spent, a Keleres agent, action cards. The prepared payment is validated again against the real question at arrival; a mismatch is Needs review, never a silent substitute.
